title: Locally finite type monomorphisms of algebraic spaces into schemes are separated and locally quasi-finite
statement: Let $S$ and $T$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], with $T$ over $S$, in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] and let $f:X\to h_T$ be an $S$-morphism, where $h_T(H)=\operatorname{Mor}_S(H,T)$. Assume $f$ is a monomorphism: $X(H)\to h_T(H)$ is injective for every $S$-scheme $H$. Assume $f$ is locally of finite type in the chartwise sense: for every representable etale map $h_V\to X$ from a scheme $V$, the composite $V\to T$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Then $f$ is separated, meaning that its diagonal $X\to X\times_{h_T}X$ becomes a closed immersion after every scheme base change [def-weil-closed-immersion], and $f$ is chartwise locally quasi-finite: for every such chart $V\to X$, the composite $V\to T$ is locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite].

source.place: Tag 0463 (lemma-monomorphism-loc-finite-type-loc-quasi-finite), specialized to a scheme target; chartwise local finite type and local quasi-finiteness are the conventions of the finite-type and quasi-finite sections.

proof.text: For every $S$-scheme $H$, a pair $(x_1,x_2)$ in $(X\times_{h_T}X)(H)$ has $f(x_1)=f(x_2)$, hence $x_1=x_2$ by monicity. The inverse to the diagonal is $(x_1,x_2)\mapsto x_1$, naturally in $H$. Explicitly, a scheme test $h_W\to X\times_{h_T}X$ is a pair $(u,v)\in X(W)^2$ with $f(u)=f(v)$, so $u=v$. The pullback of the diagonal is represented by $W$: on an $S$-scheme $H$, a map $g:H\to W$ has the unique compatible section $g^*u=g^*v$ of $X(H)$. Its projection to $W$ is the identity. By [def-weil-closed-immersion] this is a closed immersion: the whole space is closed and the structure-sheaf map is the identity. Thus $f$ is separated.

source.place: Tag 0463, separatedness sentence; elementary diagonal argument underlying lemma-monomorphism-separated

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary representable etale map $e:h_V\to X$ from a scheme, and write $q:V\to T$ for $f e$. It is locally of finite type by the hypothesis. We prove directly that $q$ is formally unramified. Let $i:H\hookrightarrow H^{\prime}$ be an affine first order thickening over $T$, and let $a,b:H^{\prime}\to V$ be two lifts over $T$ of the same $H\to V$. Since both are over $T$, $f(e a)=q a=q b=f(e b)$ in $h_T(H^{\prime})$; monicity on $H^{\prime}$ gives $e a=e b=:c$ as sections of $X(H^{\prime})$. By the representable etale condition in [def-trf-algebraic-space], $P=h_{H^{\prime}}\times_X h_V$ is a scheme and $p:P\to H^{\prime}$ is etale. The maps $s_a=(\mathrm{id},a)$ and $s_b=(\mathrm{id},b)$ satisfy $p s_a=p s_b=\mathrm{id}_{H^{\prime}}$ and $s_a i=s_b i$, so they are lifts of the same $H\to P$ over the base scheme $H^{\prime}$. By [def-weil-etale-morphism], $p$ is unramified; [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-formally-unramified] gives uniqueness of such lifts, so these sections are equal. The projection $r:P\to V$ satisfies $r s_a=a$ and $r s_b=b$, so $a=b$. Here the thickening is also over the base $H^{\prime}$ via $i$ and $\mathrm{id}_{H^{\prime}}$, exactly as required by the uniqueness theorem. This proves the affine lifting condition of [def-weil-pbc-formally-unramified-morphism].

source.place: Tag 02HE (lemma-unramified-formally-unramified); elementary uniqueness-of-lifts argument for the chart of Tag 0463

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-lft-formally-unramified-unramified] to the scheme morphism $q:V\to T$: its locally finite type hypothesis is the hypothesis of the item for this chart, and its formal unramifiedness was proved in step 2. Hence $q$ is unramified.

By [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-quasi-finite-at-points], $q$ is quasi-finite at every point of $V$, hence locally quasi-finite in the exact affine-neighbourhood sense required. The representable etale map $h_V\to X$ was arbitrary, so this proves chartwise local quasi-finiteness and completes the two conclusions.
